subject: Environment
sub_topic: Forest cover vs tree cover — distinction

concepts.name: Definition of Forest Cover: FSI Criteria and Canopy Density Threshold
key_dimensions: Minimum area criterion: 1 hectare with canopy density ≥10% — why 10% and not higher
FSI's satellite-based interpretation vs legal/statutory definition of forest
UPSC trap: Forest cover includes orchards, bamboo, and palm plantations if criteria are met
Comparison with FAO's global forest definition (0.5 ha, 10% canopy, 5m height potential)

concepts.name: Definition of Tree Cover: Patches Outside Recorded Forest Area
key_dimensions: Tree cover = trees on land parcels less than 1 hectare, outside forest cover boundary
Includes trees in urban areas, agricultural fields, roadsides, and homesteads
Not reported as 'forest' in India State of Forest Report (ISFR) forest cover statistics
UPSC trap: Total green cover = Forest cover + Tree cover; conflating the two leads to errors

concepts.name: India State of Forest Report (ISFR): Structure, Periodicity, and Reporting Agency
key_dimensions: Published biennially by Forest Survey of India (FSI), under MoEFCC
Distinction: ISFR reports forest cover and tree cover separately — not aggregated by default
Key parameters reported: Very Dense Forest, Moderately Dense Forest, Open Forest, Scrub
Recent controversy: Whether bamboo and mangrove are counted under forest or separate categories

concepts.name: Canopy Density Classes: VDF, MDF, Open Forest, and Scrub
key_dimensions: Very Dense Forest (VDF): canopy density >70%; Moderately Dense Forest (MDF): 40–70%
Open Forest: 10–40% canopy density — largest category by area in India
Scrub: canopy density <10%, NOT counted in forest cover — a common UPSC trap
Degradation trajectory: VDF → MDF → Open Forest → Scrub is a policy concern

concepts.name: Recorded Forest Area (RFA) vs Forest Cover: The Critical Overlap Problem
key_dimensions: RFA is a legal/administrative category (Reserved Forest, Protected Forest, Unclassed Forest)
Forest Cover is a remote sensing/biophysical category — the two do NOT fully overlap
Land inside RFA may have no vegetation (deforested) yet legally remains 'forest'
Land outside RFA may have dense tree cover but is NOT legally a forest — policy implication

concepts.name: Bamboo as Forest Cover: Classification Controversy and Legal Amendment
key_dimensions: Bamboo classified as 'tree' under Indian Forest Act 1927 until 2017 amendment
Indian Forest (Amendment) Act 2017: Bamboo growing outside forests reclassified as 'grass'
Impact: Bamboo outside forest land no longer requires transit permit — incentivizes cultivation
UPSC trap: Bamboo inside recorded forest area still governed by Forest Conservation Act 1980

concepts.name: Mangrove Cover: Separate Reporting within Forest Cover Framework
key_dimensions: FSI reports mangrove cover separately within forest cover (not as tree cover)
Mangroves can be Very Dense, Moderately Dense, or Open — same density classification
Coastal Regulation Zone (CRZ) notification provides separate legal protection layer
UPSC trap: Increase in mangrove area may not mean increase in 'forest cover' if density is low

concepts.name: Agroforestry and Orchards: Counted in Forest Cover or Tree Cover?
key_dimensions: Orchards and agroforestry patches >1 ha with ≥10% canopy density ARE counted in forest cover
This is a major criticism: India's forest cover increase partly driven by commercial plantations
National Agroforestry Policy 2014 aimed to expand tree cover on agricultural land
UPSC trap: Increased forest cover statistics may mask actual biodiversity loss if natural forest degrades

concepts.name: Carbon Stock vs Forest Cover: Why the Two Can Diverge
key_dimensions: Open forests have lower carbon stock per hectare despite being counted in forest cover
Dense natural forests store far more carbon than monoculture plantations of same canopy density
India's NDC commitment links to carbon sink targets — quality of forest matters, not just area
UPSC angle: Afforestation drives can increase forest cover while reducing carbon stock if native forests replaced

concepts.name: Forest Cover Change vs Net Change: Gross Loss vs Gross Gain Distinction
key_dimensions: ISFR reports net change; gross deforestation and gross afforestation may both be high simultaneously
Northeast India: High gross loss; plantation states: High gross gain — net figure masks regional disparity
UPSC trap: 'India's forest cover increased' does not mean no deforestation occurred
Global Forest Watch uses gross metrics; FSI uses net — leads to conflicting narratives

concepts.name: Forest Cover in Northeastern India: High Cover, High Loss, and Data Interpretation
key_dimensions: Northeast holds ~25% of India's forest cover despite being ~8% of land area
Jhum (shifting) cultivation cycles cause periodic fluctuation in cover — FSI captures snapshot
UPSC trap: Decrease in northeast forest cover in one ISFR doesn't necessarily mean permanent loss
Distinction: Bamboo-dominant forests in northeast may shift between 'forest' and 'non-forest' classification

concepts.name: Urban Tree Cover: Measurement, Significance, and Policy Gaps
key_dimensions: Trees in urban areas counted under 'tree cover,' not forest cover, by FSI
Urban forests (parks, avenue trees) provide ecosystem services but lack Forest Conservation Act protection
UPSC angle: Urban Heat Island mitigation through tree cover vs forest cover — different governance
No dedicated national law for urban tree cover protection — policy vacuum

concepts.name: Forest Conservation Act 1980: Applicability to Forest Cover vs RFA
key_dimensions: FCA 1980 applies to 'forest land' — Supreme Court in Godavarman case (1996) expanded to include deemed forests
Tree cover outside RFA generally NOT protected under FCA 1980 — critical policy gap
Van (Protection) Act 2023 replaced FCA 1980 — changed applicability criteria, controversy over exclusions
UPSC trap: FCA protects based on legal status, not on whether satellite shows tree cover

concepts.name: Godavarman Judgment (1996): Expanding 'Forest' Beyond Legal Boundaries
key_dimensions: Supreme Court directed that 'forest' includes all areas recorded as forest in government records, regardless of ownership
Also included areas conforming to dictionary meaning of forest — expanded beyond RFA
Impact: Some tree cover areas could be brought under FCA protection via this expansive interpretation
UPSC trap: This judgment blurs the legal line between 'forest cover' and 'tree cover' in some contexts

concepts.name: Private Forests and Tree Cover on Private Land: Regulatory Ambiguity
key_dimensions: Trees on private agricultural land counted in 'tree cover' but regulated by state tree preservation orders
Farmers often cannot fell trees on own land due to state laws — disincentivizes voluntary tree planting
Agroforestry promotion vs tree-felling restrictions: Policy contradiction affecting tree cover expansion
UPSC angle: Reform recommendations to allow felling of farm-grown trees to boost voluntary afforestation

concepts.name: National Forest Policy 1988: Forest Cover Target and Its Basis
key_dimensions: Target: 33% of India's geographical area under forest and tree cover (not just forest cover)
Current status: Forest cover ~21.7% + Tree cover ~2.9% = ~24.6% — still short of 33% target
UPSC trap: The 33% target includes BOTH forest cover AND tree cover — often misquoted as only forest cover
Hill and mountain states: 66% target for forest and tree cover under same policy

concepts.name: CAMPA Funds and Compensatory Afforestation: Forest Cover or Tree Cover Creation?
key_dimensions: Compensatory Afforestation Management and Planning Authority (CAMPA) — funds from diversion of forest land
Plantations created may qualify as 'forest cover' if >1 ha and ≥10% canopy, but biodiversity value is questioned
Non-forest land used for compensatory afforestation may create 'forest cover' in new areas
UPSC trap: CAMPA-funded plantations counted in forest cover statistics, potentially inflating 'natural forest' perception

concepts.name: Remote Sensing Technology in Forest Cover Assessment: Limitations and Accuracy
key_dimensions: FSI uses Linear Imaging Self Scanner (LISS-III) with 23.5m resolution — cannot detect small patches
Cloud cover in Northeast and Western Ghats affects data accuracy in specific reporting years
UPSC angle: Satellite cannot distinguish between natural forest and monoculture plantation of same canopy density
Comparison: Global Forest Watch uses Landsat 30m resolution — different results from FSI for same geography

concepts.name: Scrub Land: The Missing Category Between Forest Cover and Tree Cover
key_dimensions: Scrub (<10% canopy) excluded from both forest cover and tree cover in ISFR reporting
Scrubland has ecological value (dry ecosystems, wildlife habitat) but gets no policy recognition
Often converted to plantations to generate 'forest cover' — ecological replacement concern
UPSC trap: Degraded scrublands can be legally diverted without FCA clearance if not in RFA

concepts.name: Green India Mission (GIM): Targets Spanning Both Forest Cover and Tree Cover
key_dimensions: GIM under National Action Plan on Climate Change: Target to increase forest/tree cover by 5 million ha and improve quality of another 5 million ha
Explicitly addresses both forest cover AND tree cover — unlike NFP 1988 which conflates them
Funded under National Adaptation Fund — links forest cover to climate adaptation
UPSC trap: GIM's 'improving quality' component is about density enhancement, not new area — doesn't show up as area increase in ISFR
